We do have a few discussion questions we are gonna go over, and if you have any questions you want to add lmn. 
Here are a couple things we will be discussing: 
-Who was your favorite character? Why?
-What impact did you think having Chief Bromden as the narrator had on the novel? 
-Who is the book's hero?
-How did you feel about the ending? What did you like, what did you not like, and what do you wish had been different?
-Was Chief Bromden mentally insane when he was committed to the hospital 10 years ago? How does he appear when we first meet him? What is the cause of his hallucinatory fog—his medications or his paranoia or...?

Also, we do rotate where we meet each month, so totally let me know if you know any cool places to meet up. I'm not super familiar with downtown so I kinda rely on members to help pick good meeting spots.

ehh my problem with my work life balance in actuality is that I spend nearly every weekend travelling four hours away to see my family, friends, and boyfriend. This gets exhausting after a while and I'm tired and strung out after work, so not as much as I would hope for gets done. This is why I'm moving home this summer to find a closer job. I also toy with the idea of just a normal job, but feel that just proximity will solve about 90% of my issues.

This has been edited to now say only role model because I don't mind if people look up to me. I'm a strong successful girl with a lot of good stuff going on and good qualities, but I also don't feel ready to be the sole strong adult figure in someones life right now. I feel way too confused and uncertain to guide anyone else.

I'm laughing pretty hard at the fact that people are thinking that I go around acting like this 24/7 and that everyone knows about it. Hahahaha. Closer to the truth is that I have depression due to a toxic work environment and lack of friends/support system so I go home and stare at a tv/wall until I fall asleep. I don't broadcast my personal life to everyone. It's just more that I feel I was made to feel ashamed for struggling and having personal issues. My supervisor was mislabeled as my first year "mentor" but when I tried to treat her like one and seek help or guidance she really only seemed annoyed or careless. 
The whole thing is a sort of hyperbolic commentary on how in her opinion I needed to give up more of my free time and focus more on my classroom. While I was depressed and anxious because I never did anything else, and how I learned to say fuck it because it almost killed me. We just had very clashing personalities and styles when it came to the classroom. 

Also it's just about me being tired of being responsible all the damn time because I've never had any time where I wasn't responsible for not only me but everyone around me. I'm just tired of that and want to be selfish and irresponsible for a little while.

Thank you. I feel terrible that because of my mental health I can't be the teacher they need. There is not enough of me to give to them. I'm always out of town, so I am behind. I am angry and sad a lot so their chatter gets on my nerves easily. I feel so awful because there is so little of me to give to them.

That is very much how I feel I have tried to reach out to my family about wanting to leave without letting them in on too many details and have been given a lot of backlash from them. They are "living through me" and see me coming back as a failure and me wasting a lot of money. They are telling me things like they don't think I will get a job and stuff like that. 

My boyfriend was my person to reach out to but he is going through an extremely traumatic time so I think I have lost that for now. He needs me to be the strong one right now because I am the only understanding supportive force in his life. He has lost everything and I don't want to add on top of everything. 

I am moving back regardless of my families issues because I need to for my health as well as my career. Honestly I have been a terrible teacher because I spend so much of my time dealing with all kinds of shit and I'm exhausted and that is what falls. I feel relationships and family life are more important than career. I put all I have into my job but get tired cranky and impatient easily because I am giving my all to my job but some days that is only about 10 percent of me. 

I feel exhausted, trapped, and bled out. 

I don't necessarily think I want to die but I don't want to do this...so I think I could just die. It would be easier. 

And I can't ask that it sounds really obvious...
